panels.visual: The priestess of Athena Polias (older woman in a long white robe and veil, regal) holding a key and standing by the temple door
panels.caption: The priestess of Athena Polias: the most important religious office in Athens. A woman held it for life.

panels.visual: A priestess shown in four ages as a young woman, middle-aged, older, then elderly, always at the same temple, a counter of 64
panels.caption: Lysimache served for sixty-four years.

panels.visual: Athenian women in their houses at home, a girl of about fourteen at a wedding, a husband leading her away, subdued and sad mood
panels.caption: Women could not vote or own much property, and girls were often married at about fourteen.

panels.visual: A carved stone slab with the priestess' name cut into it, hand tracing the letters, next to a crowd of nameless silhouettes
panels.caption: She was one of the few women whose name was carved on monuments. Most women's names were never written down.
